categories.main_business_segments: Verisign operates as a single reportable segment focused on providing critical internet infrastructure and domain name registry services. Its core business is the operation of the authoritative registries for .com, .net, .name, certain internationalized domain names (IDN gTLDs), and the .cc country code TLD, as well as technical or back-end services for .edu and other TLDs. The company also performs Root Zone Maintainer functions and operates two of the thirteen global internet root servers.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Verisign's operations rely on a proprietary, highly secure, and distributed global infrastructure, including the Shared Registration System and the ATLAS distributed lookup system, which process hundreds of billions of DNS queries daily. The company employs advanced networking, security, and data integrity technologies, such as protected domains, distributed access control, firewalls, intrusion detection, and continuous vulnerability testing. Its infrastructure is engineered for high availability, resiliency, and rapid failover, with disaster recovery and business continuity capabilities.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Verisign's primary customers are ICANN-accredited domain name registrars, who in turn serve individual and organizational registrants seeking to establish online identities. The company’s services underpin the majority of global e-commerce and internet navigation, with end markets including businesses, individuals, and organizations worldwide that require reliable domain name resolution and registration.
categories.geographic_coverage: Verisign operates globally, with significant infrastructure in the United States (notably Virginia and Delaware) and over 200 points of presence worldwide. Its customer base spans the U.S., EMEA (Europe, Middle East, Africa), APAC (Asia-Pacific, including China, Japan, Singapore, Australia), and other regions such as Canada and Latin America. The majority of revenue is generated from U.S.-based registrars, with notable contributions from EMEA and APAC.
categories.supply_chain_position: Verisign operates as a critical infrastructure provider at the core of the internet's domain name supply chain, functioning as the authoritative registry operator (upstream) for several major TLDs. It does not directly interact with end-users but enables registrars (midstream) to offer domain registration services to registrants (downstream).
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Verisign’s strategic priorities center on maintaining and enhancing the security, stability, and resiliency of the DNS and its registry services, with significant investment in R&D for infrastructure improvements, cybersecurity, and adaptation to evolving internet protocols and standards. The company actively explores new concepts and business ideas through its innovation pipeline and collaborates with industry stakeholders to address emerging threats and regulatory requirements.
categories.revenue_model: Verisign generates revenue primarily through fixed fees charged to registrars for the initial registration and renewal of domain names in the .com, .net, and other TLDs it operates. Revenue is recognized ratably over the registration term, with pricing for .com and .net subject to contractual restrictions and periodic increases. Additional revenue streams include technical and back-end services for other TLDs and fees for Root Zone Maintainer services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Verisign faces competition from other gTLD and ccTLD registry operators such as CNNIC, DENIC, Nominet, Identity Digital, Public Interest Registry, CentralNic, Google, .xyz, GoDaddy, and Radix. Despite regulatory constraints on pricing and bundling, Verisign maintains a dominant position as the sole registry operator for .com and .net, which are the most widely used TLDs globally. The company is also challenged by alternative online identity solutions like social media and e-commerce platforms.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Verisign reported revenues of $1.56 billion (up 4% year-over-year), operating income of $1.06 billion (up 6%), and net income of $785.7 million. The company managed 169.0 million .com and .net domain registrations at year-end, a 2.1% decrease from the prior year. Verisign maintains strong cash flows from operations ($902.6 million in 2024) and a robust share repurchase program, with a market capitalization of approximately $10.3 billion as of mid-2024.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Verisign emphasizes the security, stability, and resiliency of its DNS and registry services as its core value proposition, positioning itself as a trusted steward of critical internet infrastructure. Its proprietary, highly available, and globally distributed systems ensure reliable domain name resolution and registration, supporting the majority of global e-commerce and internet navigation. The company’s longstanding relationships with ICANN and the U.S. Department of Commerce, as well as its operational expertise, further differentiate it from competitors.
